args.summary: After the latest production deploy (v2.3.1), checkout-api began failing health checks in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an error rate of ~18%. Note: v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. The service was rolled back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure and why it was promoted despite an unhealthy staging RC.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. The SEV2 incident is open as INC-0001.

**Rollback:**
- The latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an error rate of about 18%.
- v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. Rolling back to a version that has already run healthily in production didn't need change-manager approval.
- After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is about 0.2%.

**Incident:**
- INC-0001 describes the failure, the rollback and the recovery. It paged the on-call engineer.
- My first attempt to create it timed out. The incident list was still empty afterward, so I tried again using the same duplicate-protection key. You should have exactly one incident and one page.

**Follow-up:** the test version of v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging, so it shouldn't have been promoted to production. I noted this in the incident so it can be looked into along with the root cause.
